task_area: Health Maintenance, Patient Education, and Preventive Measures
front: First prenatal visit and routine pregnancy timeline: which labs, and when are GBS, Tdap and RSV given?
bottom: Type/Rh, antibody screen, CBC, HIV, syphilis, hep B, rubella.

bullets.clue: Rh-negative unsensitized: repeat antibody screen 24–28 weeks.
bullets.treat: Tdap 27–36 weeks; GBS culture 36–37 weeks; seasonal RSV 32–36.
bullets.trap: High preeclampsia risk: aspirin 81 mg after 12 weeks.

back: Type/Rh, antibody screen, CBC, HIV, syphilis, hep B, rubella. Key clue: Rh-negative unsensitized: repeat antibody screen 24–28 weeks. First-line: Tdap 27–36 weeks; GBS culture 36–37 weeks; seasonal RSV 32–36. Exam trap: High preeclampsia risk: aspirin 81 mg after 12 weeks.

diagram.alt: Prenatal timeline: first-visit labs, Rh antibody repeat at 24 to 28 weeks, Tdap 27 to 36 weeks, GBS culture 36 to 37 weeks.

source.guideline: ACOG GBS Committee Opinion 797 (2020); USPSTF Rh(D) and preeclampsia aspirin; ACOG Maternal Immunization Schedule (2026)
source.recommendation: ACOG: GBS screening 36 0/7–37 6/7 weeks. USPSTF: Rh(D) typing and antibody testing at first visit, repeat at 24–28 weeks if unsensitized Rh−; aspirin 81 mg after 12 weeks for high preeclampsia risk. ACOG 2026 schedule: Tdap 27–36 weeks, RSV 32 0/7–36 6/7 weeks in season.

front: Positive hCG, pelvic pain, no intrauterine pregnancy on ultrasound: diagnosis and who gets methotrexate?
bottom: Ectopic until proven otherwise; stable and unruptured can get methotrexate.

bullets.clue: hCG above discriminatory zone with empty uterus.
bullets.treat: Methotrexate if stable; surgery if unstable or rupture.
bullets.trap: hCG >5,000, cardiac activity, mass >4 cm favor surgery.

back: Ectopic until proven otherwise; stable and unruptured can get methotrexate. Key clue: hCG above discriminatory zone with empty uterus. First-line: Methotrexate if stable; surgery if unstable or rupture. Exam trap: hCG >5,000, cardiac activity, mass >4 cm favor surgery.

diagram.alt: Ectopic pregnancy: positive hCG with empty uterus; stable unruptured gets methotrexate, unstable goes to surgery.

source.guideline: ACOG Practice Bulletin 193: Tubal Ectopic Pregnancy (still current as of 2026)
source.recommendation: ACOG PB 193: methotrexate for hemodynamically stable unruptured tubal ectopic without absolute contraindications; hCG >5,000, fetal cardiac activity and mass >4 cm are relative contraindications; surgery for instability or rupture.

task_area: History Taking and Performing Physical Examination
front: Third-trimester vaginal bleeding: which history and exam findings separate placenta previa from abruption, and what exam must you avoid?
bottom: Painless bleeding: previa. Painful bleeding with a tender uterus: abruption.

bullets.clue: Previa: placenta over os on ultrasound.
bullets.treat: Stabilize, ultrasound first, fetal monitoring, delivery planning.
bullets.trap: No digital cervical exam until previa excluded.

back: Painless bleeding: previa. Painful bleeding with a tender uterus: abruption. Key clue: Previa: placenta over os on ultrasound. First-line: Stabilize, ultrasound first, fetal monitoring, delivery planning. Exam trap: No digital cervical exam until previa excluded.

diagram.alt: Third-trimester bleeding: painless suggests previa, painful suggests abruption; ultrasound before any digital exam.

source.guideline: ACR Appropriateness Criteria: Second and Third Trimester Vaginal Bleeding; ACOG/SMFM Obstetric Care Consensus 7 (Placenta Accreta Spectrum) (still current as of 2026)
source.recommendation: ACR: ultrasound is the mainstay; digital pelvic exam should be avoided until previa, low-lying placenta and vasa previa are excluded; transvaginal US is accurate and safe for previa. ACOG/SMFM OCC 7: previa plus prior cesarean is the key accreta risk.

front: 35-year-old smoker of 20 cigarettes a day wants birth control: which methods are unsafe and what is emergency contraception?

bullets.treat: IUD, implant, DMPA or progestin pill; copper IUD most effective EC.
bullets.trap: Migraine with aura and <21 days postpartum are also CHC category 4.

back: Combined hormonal contraception is category 4. Key clue: Age ≥35 and ≥15 cigarettes/day. First-line: IUD, implant, DMPA or progestin pill; copper IUD most effective EC. Exam trap: Migraine with aura and <21 days postpartum are also CHC category 4.

diagram.alt: US MEC 2024: combined hormonal contraception unacceptable for smokers 35 or older using 15 or more cigarettes daily; progestin and IUD methods acceptable.

source.guideline: CDC US Medical Eligibility Criteria (US MEC) 2024; US Selected Practice Recommendations (US SPR) 2024
source.recommendation: US MEC 2024: CHC category 4 for age ≥35 smoking ≥15/day, migraine with aura, <21 days postpartum; other methods category 1. US SPR 2024: Cu-IUD within 5 days as EC; UPA 30 mg or LNG 1.5 mg.

task_area: Health Maintenance, Patient Education, and Preventive Measures
front: Routine pregnancy at 24–28 weeks: how is gestational diabetes screened and what is first-line drug therapy?
bottom: Screen at 24–28 weeks; insulin if lifestyle fails.

bullets.clue: Two-step 50 g then 100 g, or one-step 75 g OGTT.
bullets.treat: Nutrition and activity first; insulin preferred drug.
bullets.trap: Metformin and glyburide cross the placenta; not first-line.

back: Screen at 24–28 weeks; insulin if lifestyle fails. Key clue: Two-step 50 g then 100 g, or one-step 75 g OGTT. First-line: Nutrition and activity first; insulin preferred drug. Exam trap: Metformin and glyburide cross the placenta; not first-line.

diagram.alt: Gestational diabetes: screen at 24 to 28 weeks, lifestyle first, insulin preferred over metformin or glyburide.

source.guideline: USPSTF Gestational Diabetes: Screening (2021); ACOG Clinical Practice Update (2024); ADA Standards of Care 2025 section 15
source.recommendation: USPSTF 2021: screen at ≥24 weeks (B). ACOG 2024: one- or two-step acceptable. ADA 2025: lifestyle first; insulin preferred; metformin and glyburide not first-line (cross placenta).

task_area: Health Maintenance, Patient Education, and Preventive Measures
front: Average-risk 32-year-old asks how often she needs cervical cancer screening.
bottom: Ages 30–65: HPV every 5 years (or cytology every 3).

bullets.treat: Primary HPV, cotesting or cytology by age interval.
bullets.trap: No screening under 21 or after hysterectomy with cervix removed.

back: Ages 30–65: HPV every 5 years (or cytology every 3). Key clue: 21–29: cytology every 3 years. First-line: Primary HPV, cotesting or cytology by age interval. Exam trap: No screening under 21 or after hysterectomy with cervix removed.

diagram.alt: Cervical screening: no screening before 21, cytology every 3 years 21 to 29, HPV every 5 years 30 to 65.

source.guideline: USPSTF Cervical Cancer: Screening (final 2018; draft update Dec 2024) (still current as of 2026)
source.recommendation: USPSTF: cytology q3y ages 21–29; ages 30–65 hrHPV q5y, cotesting q5y or cytology q3y; D for <21, >65 with adequate screening, hysterectomy without CIN2+. 2024 draft adds patient-collected HPV.

task_area: Health Maintenance, Patient Education, and Preventive Measures
front: Breast cancer screening at 40, and first imaging for a palpable mass by age.

bullets.clue: Mass: ultrasound under 30; 30–39 ultrasound or mammogram; 40+ mammogram.
bullets.treat: Image, then biopsy any suspicious mass.
bullets.trap: Supplemental MRI or ultrasound for dense breasts: insufficient evidence (I).

back: Biennial mammography ages 40–74. Key clue: Mass: ultrasound under 30; 30–39 ultrasound or mammogram; 40+ mammogram. First-line: Image, then biopsy any suspicious mass. Exam trap: Supplemental MRI or ultrasound for dense breasts: insufficient evidence (I).

diagram.alt: Breast: biennial mammography 40 to 74; palpable mass ultrasound under 30 and diagnostic mammography 40 and older.

source.guideline: USPSTF Breast Cancer: Screening (2024); ACR Appropriateness Criteria Palpable Breast Masses (2022)
source.recommendation: USPSTF 2024: biennial mammography 40–74 (B); ≥75 and dense-breast supplemental imaging I. ACR 2022 narrative: ultrasound initial under 30; 30–39 (variant 11) ultrasound, diagnostic mammography or DBT all usually appropriate; diagnostic mammography/DBT at ≥40; suspicious exam with negative imaging still needs biopsy.

task_area: History Taking and Performing Physical Examination
front: Sexually active woman with lower abdominal pain: which pelvic exam findings support PID, and what do you do next?
bottom: Cervical motion, uterine or adnexal tenderness: treat PID empirically.

bullets.clue: Minimal criteria suffice; do not wait for cultures.
bullets.treat: Ceftriaxone 500 mg IM plus doxycycline and metronidazole 14 days.
bullets.trap: Delaying treatment risks infertility and ectopic pregnancy.

back: Cervical motion, uterine or adnexal tenderness: treat PID empirically. Key clue: Minimal criteria suffice; do not wait for cultures. First-line: Ceftriaxone 500 mg IM plus doxycycline and metronidazole 14 days. Exam trap: Delaying treatment risks infertility and ectopic pregnancy.

diagram.alt: PID: cervical motion tenderness, treat with ceftriaxone plus 14 days of doxycycline and metronidazole.

source.guideline: CDC STI Treatment Guidelines 2021: PID, BV, trichomoniasis
source.recommendation: CDC 2021: PID outpatient ceftriaxone 500 mg IM once + doxycycline 100 mg BID 14 d + metronidazole 500 mg BID 14 d. BV (Amsel ≥3/4) metronidazole 500 mg BID 7 d. Trich (women) metronidazole 500 mg BID 7 d.

front: 47-year-old with heavy irregular bleeding: classification system and first workup step?
bottom: Classify by PALM-COEIN; endometrial sampling if over 45.

bullets.clue: Pregnancy test first, then CBC and ultrasound.
bullets.treat: Hormonal therapy or LNG-IUD for ovulatory/anovulatory AUB once cancer excluded.
bullets.trap: Under 45 with obesity or unopposed estrogen also needs biopsy.

back: Classify by PALM-COEIN; endometrial sampling if over 45. Key clue: Pregnancy test first, then CBC and ultrasound. First-line: Hormonal therapy or LNG-IUD for ovulatory/anovulatory AUB once cancer excluded. Exam trap: Under 45 with obesity or unopposed estrogen also needs biopsy.

diagram.alt: Abnormal uterine bleeding: PALM-COEIN classification; endometrial sampling first-line over age 45.

source.guideline: ACOG Practice Bulletin 128 (AUB, reaffirmed) and Committee Opinion 557 (still current as of 2026)
source.recommendation: ACOG: PALM-COEIN classification; endometrial sampling first-line for AUB at >45 and for younger women with unopposed estrogen exposure, failed management or persistent AUB.

front: Vaginal discharge: how do pH, whiff test and wet mount separate bacterial vaginosis, trichomoniasis and Candida, and what treats each?
bottom: BV: pH >4.5, clue cells. Trichomonas: motile organisms. Candida: normal pH, hyphae.

bullets.treat: BV, trichomonas: metronidazole 7 days. Candida: fluconazole 150 mg once.
bullets.trap: Treat trichomonas partners; negative wet mount does not exclude it.

back: BV: pH >4.5, clue cells. Trichomonas: motile organisms. Candida: normal pH, hyphae. Key clue: Candida: thick curdy discharge. First-line: BV, trichomonas: metronidazole 7 days. Candida: fluconazole 150 mg once. Exam trap: Treat trichomonas partners; negative wet mount does not exclude it.

diagram.alt: Vaginal discharge: bacterial vaginosis has pH above 4.5 and clue cells, trichomoniasis shows motile organisms, Candida has normal pH and hyphae; metronidazole for BV and trichomonas, fluconazole for Candida.

source.guideline: CDC Sexually Transmitted Infections Treatment Guidelines, 2021: bacterial vaginosis, trichomoniasis and vulvovaginal candidiasis
source.recommendation: CDC 2021: BV diagnosed by clinical (Amsel) or Gram-stain criteria including pH >4.5, clue cells and positive whiff test; trichomonas by NAAT or motile organisms on wet mount, microscopy sensitivity about 50%; metronidazole 500 mg twice daily for 7 days for BV and for trichomoniasis in women; sex partners of trichomoniasis patients should be treated; women with trichomoniasis retested about 3 months after treatment; VVC treated with topical azole or fluconazole 150 mg single dose.

front: Why are cycles irregular in many patients with PCOS, and which induction drug is first-line?
bottom: Insulin resistance and excess LH drive ovarian androgen production.

bullets.clue: Two of three: oligo-ovulation, hyperandrogenism, polycystic ovaries.
bullets.treat: 2023 international PCOS guideline: letrozole is first-line for ovulation induction.
bullets.trap: A normal ultrasound does not exclude PCOS.

back: Insulin resistance and excess LH drive ovarian androgen production. Key clue: Two of three: oligo-ovulation, hyperandrogenism, polycystic ovaries. First-line: 2023 international PCOS guideline: letrozole is first-line for ovulation induction. Exam trap: A normal ultrasound does not exclude PCOS.

diagram.alt: Insulin resistance and excess LH drive ovarian androgen production.

source.guideline: 2023 International Evidence-based Guideline for the Assessment and Management of PCOS
source.recommendation: 2023 guideline: Rotterdam criteria (2 of 3) in adults, AMH may replace ultrasound; letrozole first-line pharmacological ovulation induction over clomiphene; screen metabolic risk.

front: Boggy uterus and heavy bleeding after delivery: cause and first-line treatment?
bottom: Uterine atony, most common cause of postpartum hemorrhage.

bullets.treat: Uterine massage and oxytocin; tranexamic acid early.
bullets.trap: TXA benefit is clearest within 3 hours of birth.

back: Uterine atony, most common cause of postpartum hemorrhage. Key clue: 4 Ts: tone, trauma, tissue, thrombin. First-line: Uterine massage and oxytocin; tranexamic acid early. Exam trap: TXA benefit is clearest within 3 hours of birth.

diagram.alt: Postpartum hemorrhage: atony is most common; massage, oxytocin and early tranexamic acid.

source.guideline: ACOG Practice Bulletin 183: Postpartum Hemorrhage (still current as of 2026)
source.recommendation: ACOG PB 183: routine postpartum oxytocin; 4 Ts; atony 70–80%; massage, bladder emptying, uterotonics; consider TXA when initial therapy fails, most benefit within 3 hours.

front: Newborn with jaundice at 18 hours of life: what to do next?
bottom: Jaundice under 24 hours is pathologic until proven otherwise.

bullets.clue: Visible jaundice in first day of life.
bullets.treat: Measure TSB or TcB now; phototherapy by hour-specific thresholds.
bullets.trap: Don't rely on visual estimate; plot bilirubin by age in hours.

back: Jaundice under 24 hours is pathologic until proven otherwise. Key clue: Visible jaundice in first day of life. First-line: Measure TSB or TcB now; phototherapy by hour-specific thresholds. Exam trap: Don't rely on visual estimate; plot bilirubin by age in hours.

diagram.alt: Newborn jaundice before 24 hours: measure bilirubin promptly and treat per hour-specific thresholds.

source.guideline: AAP Clinical Practice Guideline: Hyperbilirubinemia in the Newborn ≥35 Weeks (2022)
source.recommendation: AAP 2022: assess jaundice at least every 12 h; jaundice <24 h requires TSB/TcB as soon as possible; otherwise TcB/TSB at 24–48 h or before discharge; phototherapy by hour-specific thresholds.
